parameters_passed_to_the_search_agent.search_scope: Dutch national subsidies, loans and other financing run by RVO that are open or about to open and are relevant to the energy sector in any way: energy and climate innovation (the Energy Innovation NL schemes, for example MOOI and DEI+), electricity grids, offshore wind, storage and flexibility, hydrogen, industrial electrification and sustainability, digitalisation, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity (for example CIF-NL), and general innovation financing (for example the Innovatiekrediet). Skip schemes only for households, agriculture, fisheries, nature or housing, and pages that are permits, registrations or import and export procedures. RVO pages that only explain an EU programme and send applicants to the EU Funding & Tenders Portal are covered by that source; record them here only when RVO runs a national scheme with its own budget or application period (for example national co-financing). Cascade funding calls of EU-funded projects are covered by the EU Funding & Tenders Portal source, even when an RVO page mentions one.
parameters_passed_to_the_search_agent.navigation_instructions: 1. The results list loads with JavaScript. A plain page fetch returns only the introduction text, so use a browser. 2. Open the starting URL. It is sorted by title (A to Z) and filtered on two status values (status=3294,3295). Check in the status filter that these are 'Open voor aanvragen' and 'Bijna open voor aanvragen' (opens within one month); if the selected labels differ, select those two yourself. 'Tijdelijk gesloten' and 'Gesloten' are out of scope. 3. Work through the whole list to the last result, through every page or 'Load more'. Screen each scheme by its title and short description against the search scope. 4. Open each relevant scheme page (www.rvo.nl/subsidies-financiering/<scheme>). It shows the status, the budget and maximum subsidy ('Hoogte financiering en budget'), the application period, who can apply, and 'Wetten en regels' with a link to the regulation in the Staatscourant. Sub-pages hold the conditions, the application steps ('Aanvragen') and the questions and answers. 5. Some schemes have several themes or rounds, each with its own budget or application period (for example the DEI+ themes). Treat each of those as its own FO, using the scheme page and the theme page. 6. The Staatscourant regulation is the authoritative text for eligibility, subsidy rates and deadlines. A 'Bijna open' scheme may give only a planned opening date; record it as forthcoming. 7. The pages are in Dutch. english.rvo.nl has English versions of some pages, but the Dutch page is authoritative. 8. Each page states 'De inhoud van deze pagina is gecontroleerd op <date>'. Use that date to see whether a known scheme page has changed since its FO record was saved.
parameters_passed_to_the_search_agent.link_scope: Scheme pages and their sub-pages under www.rvo.nl/subsidies-financiering/, their English versions on english.rvo.nl, and the regulation texts they link to on zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl and wetten.overheid.nl. Do not follow links to eLoket or login pages, other RVO sections (registrations, permits, import and export), news, events, or external programme websites.
parameters_passed_to_the_search_agent.completion_rules: The run is complete when the last result of the alphabetical list has been screened and every relevant scheme page, with its theme pages, has been opened. If the run reaches the cap of 5 new candidates first, stop there: later runs skip the schemes already recorded and find the rest. A run that screens everything and finds no new scheme ends with no new FO.
